scale_convert.note: A 28 mm figure measured feet-to-eyes of a 1780 mm person. Makers disagree on the convention (Wikipedia 'Miniature wargame'); heroic figures also exaggerate heads, hands and weapons, so use the ratio for vehicles and terrain, not anatomy.

limits.basis: Formlabs Design Guide (SLA, Clear resin, 100 um layers); hobby MSLA printers at 0.03-0.05 mm often hold finer detail, so these limits are conservative. Fit clearances are a hobby convention, not from the guide: print a stepped tolerance coupon on your printer and resin before trusting them.

scale_convert.estimate_kind: HEURISTIC: process limits from the cited design guides; thicken (heroic exaggeration) or drop features below them. Walls use the unsupported-wall limit.

base.note: Standard sizes follow the Games Workshop base range (round 25-160 mm, oval 60x35-170x105) that most tabletop games use; ~3-4.5 mm tall with a bevelled rim. Measure a commercial base if the game cares.

key.why: a flat (or a second peg) lets the joint go together one way only

checks.name: peg prints as a free-standing pin
checks.basis: Formlabs wire table (0.3 mm/7 mm to 1.5 mm/30 mm): stubby pegs survive printing, washing and assembly.

checks.name: wall around the socket
checks.basis: Material left around the socket in the receiving part (unsupported-wall limit).

base_and_peg.clearances_basis: Formlabs Design Guide (SLA, Clear resin, 100 um layers); hobby MSLA printers at 0.03-0.05 mm often hold finer detail, so these limits are conservative. Fit clearances are a hobby convention, not from the guide: print a stepped tolerance coupon on your printer and resin before trusting them.
base_and_peg.estimate_kind: HEURISTIC fits: print a stepped tolerance coupon (pockets and sockets in 0.05 mm steps) first.

support_plan.score: max layer area / as-modelled + 0.5 x support area / as-modelled + 0.25 x support starts / as-modelled (lower is better)

printability.basis: Formlabs Design Guide (SLA, Clear resin, 100 um layers); hobby MSLA printers at 0.03-0.05 mm often hold finer detail, so these limits are conservative. Fit clearances are a hobby convention, not from the guide: print a stepped tolerance coupon on your printer and resin before trusting them.

checks.name: closed (watertight)
checks.basis: Every edge shared by exactly two triangles (trimesh is_watertight); slicers guess at open meshes.

checks.name: manifold
checks.basis: No edge shared by more than two triangles (touching bodies, tangent booleans).

checks.name: consistent winding
checks.basis: Neighbouring triangles must wind the same way so inside and outside are defined.

checks.name: separate bodies
checks.basis: Disconnected shells print as separate pieces or loose islands; split them into parts or join them.

checks.name: no enclosed voids
checks.basis: Sealed cavities trap uncured resin that later cracks the part: add a drain hole (>= 3.5 mm, Formlabs) and a vent, as PrusaSlicer SLA hollowing does.

checks.name: minimum wall (supported)
checks.limit: <= 0.5 mm2 thinner than 0.4 mm
checks.basis: Formlabs: walls connected on two or more sides >= 0.4 mm; thinner walls warp on peel. Small areas at tips and edges are tolerated.

checks.name: minimum wall (unsupported)
checks.limit: <= 0.5 mm2 thinner than 0.6 mm
checks.basis: Formlabs: walls connected on fewer than two sides >= 0.6 mm. Thin spots listed here are fine only if braced on two sides.

checks.name: thin spikes / wires
checks.limit: none longer than the process wire table allows
checks.basis: Formlabs: a wire (length > 2 x width) holds 0.3 mm up to 7 mm tall and 1.5 mm up to 30 mm; longer ones wave or snap. Detected along the print z axis only; horizontal pins show up as thin walls.

checks.name: suction cups
checks.limit: <= 10.0 mm2 sealed layer area
checks.basis: A cavity the vat film seals while it peels (Lychee/CHITUBOX 'suction cup') pulls the part off its supports or deforms it. Vent it sideways or toward the plate, or re-orient. The default limit is a heuristic; 0 flags every cup.

checks.name: overhangs needing support
checks.limit: downward faces flatter than 19.0 deg from level
checks.basis: Formlabs: unsupported overhangs >= 19 deg from level (resin); the Prusa KB 'overhang threshold' is measured the same way (45 deg is the usual FDM rule).

checks.name: islands
checks.basis: A layer region with nothing under it (CHITUBOX/Lychee island detection) needs a support there.

checks.name: fits build volume
checks.basis: Bounding box in print orientation vs the printer build volume.

printability.method: Edge topology after welding to 0.1 um; shells and cavities by edge-connected groups with ray parity; wall thickness by inward-normal ray casting from triangle centroids; islands, suction cups, voids and wires on a ray-cast voxel model (rows along x, exact in x, voxel_mm in y and z). z up = away from the build plate.
printability.estimate_kind: HEURISTIC printability screen, not a slicer: confirm supports and suction in your slicer (Lychee, CHITUBOX, PrusaSlicer) and print a test piece.

support_plan.score: max layer area / as-modelled + 0.5 x support area / as-modelled + 0.25 x support starts / as-modelled (lower is better)
